svg.title: OpenStack Lab — Full Installation Map
svg.desc: A privacy-safe architecture overview and one ordered thirteen-step Kolla-Ansible installation path.
svg.text: Fresh Ubuntu → tested cloud → optional extensions
Separate deployment host · three multi-role nodes
Deployment host only · SSH · Ansible · Kolla CLI
PROVIDER L2 · NO HOST IP · VERIFY CABLING
Reserved on management network · Keepalived / HAProxy

text.tspan: All three nodes carry control, network, and compute roles.
Verify NIC identity and cable path before assigning provider L2.
Choose an unused VIP locally; no real address is shown.
Monitoring/storage hosts are selected only when enabling them.
Local Cinder LVM is not replicated high-availability storage.

svg.text: Read the failing task · change one cause at a time
Follow Step 1 through Step 13; extensions come after a tested core cloud.
Management VM and all three nodes; protect any data disks.
Install the SSH server on nodes; connect from the management VM.
Ansible 13–14 and stable/2026.2 in a dedicated Python venv.
Verify NICs; set management/provider L2; reserve an unused VIP.
All nodes in control/network/compute; remove active sample hosts.
Use consistent name resolution and synchronized clocks.
Set interfaces/VIP; generate passwords and keep them private.
Let Kolla prepare hosts; fix failures instead of bypassing them.
Run deploy, then validate-config; preserve logs if a task fails.
Check token/services, then boot one small VM on a private network.
Choose a backend and safe storage device; local LVM is not HA.
Add only after the manual cloud test; protect application credentials.
Select real monitoring hosts, then enable after the core cloud is stable.

text.tspan: Kolla prechecks are required deployment gates—not a replacement
for installing Ubuntu, SSH, Ansible, and Kolla-Ansible.

svg.text: REVIEW COPY · Generic labels only · Companion to the FULL installation guide
